g.text: Down Home Creole · Phase 1 · P1-404 Wrap labeler for round containers (built in house) · rev B
NEC 430, UL 508A practice; 75 °C Cu; cord-and-plug; 24 V SELV control
UNLESS NOTED: LINEAR ±0.5 [±.02] · HOLES +0.2/-0 · ANGLES ±0.5° · MACHINED X.X ±0.1, X.XX ±0.05 · THIRD-ANGLE PROJECTION · BREAK EDGES 0.5 · ASME Y14.5

svg.text: SUPPLY 120 V 1-ph 60 Hz, cord and plug, 15/20 A receptacle on the bench (≈ 1.2 A max); control and motor 24 V DC
L black / N white / PE green
0V bonded to PE at TB2 (one point)
M-0 → M1 (W2): enable, step, dir, HLFB
PE: cord green → TB1 PE → PE stud → G1 earth, M1 body (W1), base via the bench bolts, lid and end-wall operators via the strap. < 0.1 Ω PE stud to the -x plate (ITP).
HOW THE CIRCUIT AND PROGRAM WORK
S1 ON powers G1; A1 boots and enables M1 (HLFB high = ready). H1 flashes until a gap has been found: press FEED, the web advances slowly to the next gap and stops (H1 steady).
The operator lays the container on the rollers against the fence and lowers the idler arm: B2 closes (arm down), and after 0.3 s A1 runs M1 up to speed (ramp 0.15 s) for one label.
A1 counts steps from the start and arms the gap input only after 90 % of the label pitch (S 193 / J 258); the first dark pulse on B1 then stops M1 with a 0.1 s ramp.
If no gap appears by 120 % of the pitch, A1 stops M1 and flashes H1 fast (web broken, roll empty or wrong S/J setting). FEED clears the fault after the web is fixed.
E-stop S0 opens the AC feed to G1 (two NC contacts in series, stop category 0); the 24 V bus falls in < 0.1 s, M1 de-energises and coasts (< 0.1 s, low inertia). Twist to release, then FEED.
Lifting the arm mid-label (B2 opens) stops M1 at once (hand-safe: the nip is between the rollers and the container, 0.07 N·m motor torque, no pinch force > 15 N).
4 x Ø22.5 [.886] in the end wall; 50 pitch rows
glands G1-G4 M20 low on the same wall
A1 CLEARCORE on the floor (136 x 106), 4 x M3
Cord SJOOW 14/3 3 m + NEMA 5-15P, gland M20 (P1-456)
plant receptacle on the bench, 15/20 A
E-stop 40 mm mushroom, twist release, 2 NC (P1-456)
FEED push button illuminated green 24 V, 1 NO (P1-456)
Power supply 120 V AC → 24 V DC 6.5 A (P1-426)
DIN terminals 24 V: +24 x 6, 0 V x 6 (P1-456)
Gap sensor fork 40, PNP NO (dark = gap), M8 4-pin (P1-427)
Start sensor inductive M12 PNP NO 4 mm (P1-457)
rising edge + 0.3 s → run one label
jog to next gap; clears faults
flash = no gap yet; fast = fault
PE stud on the back wall
base bonded via the bench bolts
both -V screws; 0 V to PE at TB2 (one point)
W3 → B2: brown +24, blue 0V, black → A1 DI-6
W4 → B1: brown +24, blue 0V, black → A1 DI-7, white (teach) n.c.
G2 M20, along the base under the -x plate
G3 M20 (split grommet for the plug)
78.5 mm of container surface per rev
needed ≈ 0.07 N·m; limit keeps a jam soft
SDSK runs 24-75 V; 24 V caps top speed well above the need
1. Load: G1 156 W max → ≈ 1.2 A at 120 V; F1 3 A time-delay protects the cord and G1 (inrush < 65 A cold, T fuse rides it).
2. Keep W2/W3/W4 apart from W0 inside the box; sensor cables on the base in a 304 clip under the -x plate edge, clear of the rollers and belts.
3. E-stop removes AC from G1 (two NC). The 24 V bus discharges in < 0.1 s with M1 enabled; a monitored stop is not needed at 0.07 N·m (risk assessment in the ITP).
4. Program P1-404-FW-01 (ClearCore Arduino) is kept with the plant software; the S/J pitch and step scale come from design.py at build time.
